L934: ###### Theorem \the\thmnumbering.
L935: 
L936: Let $(u_{j})_{j\in J}$ be a net of classically psh functions on the $k$-analytic space $X$ which converges pointwise to an upper semicontinuous function $u$. Then $u$ is classically psh.
L937: For a sequence of semipositive ${\mathbf{R}}$-PL functions converging pointwise to an ${\mathbf{R}}$-PL function, the above result was shown in [【50†GR25】, Theorem 5.6]. When $X$ is a proper algebraic variety, this was known before ([【129†GK19】, Proposition 7.2] for uniform limits, [【71†GM19】, Theorem 1.3] for pointwise limits).
L938: ###### Proof.
L939: Since $u$ is upper semicontinuous, using the definition of classically psh functions, we may assume that $X$ is a connected smooth curve over a non-trivially valued field. We may assume that $u$ is not identically $-\infty$. Then for every strictly $k$-affinoid domain $U$ of $X$ and every harmonic function $h$ on $U$ with $u\leq h$ on $\partial U$, we have to show that $u\leq h$ holds on $U$.
L940: Since $u_{j}\to u$ pointwise and since $\partial U$ is finite, for any $\varepsilon>0$ we have $u_{j}-h\leq\varepsilon$ on $\partial U$ for all $j$ sufficiently large. Since $u_{j}-h$ is a classically psh function by Proposition 【30†3】(【91†4】) and since the Shilov boundary of $U$ agrees with $\partial U$ [【40†Thu05】, §2.1.2], the global affinoid maximum principle in Theorem 【33†6】 shows that $u_{j}-h\leq\varepsilon$ on $U$ for all $j$ sufficiently large.
L941: It follows that $u-h\leq\varepsilon$ on $U$, which implies $u\leq h$ on $U$ since $\varepsilon$ was arbitrary. ∎
L942: ## 7. Pluriharmonic functions
L943: 
L944: In this section, we consider a $k$-analytic space $X$ over any non-Archimedean field $k$. Following the discussion of harmonic functions on curves in 【98†3.5】, we generalize this notion as follows to higher dimensions.
L945: 
L946: ###### Definition \the\thmnumbering.
L947: 
L948: A function $h\colon X\to{\mathbf{R}}$ is called pluriharmonic if $h$ and $-h$ are classically psh functions (see Definition 【31†4】).
L949: ###### Proposition \the\thmnumbering.
L950: 
L951: Pluriharmonic functions are continuous and have the properties:
L952: 
L953:   1. (1)
L954: 
L955: (Sheafiness) The pluriharmonic functions form a sheaf on $X$.
L956: 
L957:   2. (2)
L958: 
L959: If $f\in\Gamma(X,{\mathscr{O}}_{X}^{\times})$ then $\log|f|$ is pluriharmonic.
L960: 
L961:   3. (3)
L962: 
L963: (Vector Space) The pluriharmonic functions on $X$ form a real vector space which we denote by $\operatorname{PH}(X)$.
L964: 
L965:   4. (4)
L966: (Limits) If a function $h\colon X\to{\mathbf{R}}$ is locally a uniform limit of pluriharmonic functions, then $h$ is pluriharmonic.
L967: 
L968:   5. (5)
L969: 
L970: (Maximum Principle) If $h\in\operatorname{PH}(X)$ and $h$ attains a local extremum at $x\in\operatorname{Int}(X)$, then $h$ is constant in a neighborhood of $x$.
L971: 
L972:   6. (6)
L973: 
L974: (Extension of Scalars) Let $k^{\prime}/k$ be an analytic extension field. Then $h$ pluriharmonic if and only if $h\circ\pi_{k^{\prime}/k}\colon X_{k^{\prime}}\to{\mathbf{R}}$ is pluriharmonic.
L975:   7. (7)
L976: 
L977: (Functoriality) Let $Y$ be a $k$-analytic space and let $f\colon Y\to X$ be a morphism. If $h\in\operatorname{PH}(X)$ then $h\circ f\in\operatorname{PH}(Y)$, and the converse holds if $f$ is finite and surjective.
L978: ###### Proof.
L979: It is clear that a pluriharmonic function $h$ is continuous as $h$ and $-h$ are upper semicontinuous. Properties (【130†1】), (【131†2】), (【132†3】), (【133†6】) and (【134†7】) follow immediately from the corresponding properties of classically psh functions given in Proposition 【31†4】. In (【135†4】), we note that a uniform limit of pluriharmonic functions can be easily written as a decreasing (resp. increasing) limit of pluriharmonic functions and hence (【135†4】) follows from Proposition 【31†4】(【105†4】).
L980: The maximum principle (【136†5】) follows from the maximum principle for classically psh functions shown in Theorem 【33†6】. ∎
L981: From now on, we denote by $\operatorname{PH}(X)$ the space of pluriharmonic functions on $X$. The affinoid global maximum principle for classically psh functions has the following consequence.
L982: ###### Proposition \the\thmnumbering.
L983: 
L984: Let $X$ be a $k$-affinoid space with Shilov boundary $\Gamma$. Then every pluriharmonic function takes its global maximum and its global minimum in a Shilov point of $X$, and the ${\mathbf{R}}$-linear map
L985: 
L986:  | $$\operatorname{PH}(X)\longrightarrow{\mathbf{R}}^{\Gamma},\quad h\mapsto(h(x))_{x\in\Gamma}$$  |
L987: 
L988: is injective.
L989: ###### Proof.
L990: 
L991: By definition, the function $h\colon X\to{\mathbf{R}}$ is pluriharmonic if and only if $h$ and $-h$ are classically psh. It follows from Theorem 【33†6】 that a pluriharmonic function takes its maximum and its minimum on the Shilov boundary $\Gamma$. In particular, a pluriharmonic function is zero if and only if its restriction to $\Gamma$ is zero, which proves the last claim. ∎
L992: ###### Theorem \the\thmnumbering.
L993: 
L994: Let $X$ be a quasicompact $k$-analytic space. Then $\operatorname{PH}(X)$ is a finite dimensional real vector space.
L995: ###### Proof.
L996: 
L997: Using quasicompactness, we can cover $X$ by finitely affinoid subsets $U_{i}$. Using Proposition 【34†7】, we know that $\operatorname{PH}(U_{i})$ is finite dimensional for every $i$. Since pluriharmonic functions are determined by their restrictions to the $U_{i}$’s, this proves the claim. For later purposes, we note that the linear map
L998: 
L999: (10)  |  | $$\operatorname{PH}(X)\longrightarrow{\mathbf{R}}^{\Gamma},\quad h\mapsto(h(x))_{x\in\Gamma}$$  |
L1000: is injective where $\Gamma$ is the union of the Shilov boundaries of all $U_{i}$’s. ∎
L1001: ###### Remark \the\thmnumbering.
L1002: 
L1003: Assume that $k$ is non-trivially valued and that $X$ is a quasicompact $k$-analytic space. Let ${\mathfrak{X}}$ be any formal model of $X$ over the valuation ring $k^{\circ}$. Then $\dim(\operatorname{PH}(X))$ is bounded by the number of divisorial points of $X$ associated to ${\mathfrak{X}}$.
L1004: Indeed, such a formal model is quasi-compact, hence can be covered by finitely many formal affine open subsets ${\mathfrak{U}}_{i}$. Then the above argument applies to the strictly affinoid covering $U_{i}={\mathfrak{U}}_{i,\eta}$ of $X$. Let $\Gamma$ be the set of divisorial points associated to ${\mathfrak{X}}$. This is just the union of the Shilov points of the $U_{i}$’s [【71†GM19】, Proposition A.3]. Injectivity of (【137†10】) leads to the desired bound.
L1005: ###### Theorem \the\thmnumbering.
L1006: 
L1007: Let $X$ be a $k$-analytic space over any non-Archimedean field $k$, and let $f\colon X\to{\mathbf{R}}$ be a continuous function. If $f$ is the pointwise limit of a sequence of pluriharmonic functions on $X$, then the convergence is locally uniform and $f$ is a pluriharmonic function.
L1008: ###### Proof.
L1009: 
L1010: This is a local statement, so we may assume that $X$ is quasicompact. Using the notation from the proof of Theorem 【34†7】, injectivity of (【137†10】) shows that
L1011: 
L1012:  | $$\|h\|=\sup_{x\in\Gamma}|h(x)|$$  |
L1013: defines a norm on the finite dimensional ${\mathbf{R}}$-vector space $\operatorname{PH}(X)$. Let $h_{m}$ be a sequence of pluriharmonic functions converging pointwise to $f$. Then $h_{m}$ converges to some $h\in\operatorname{PH}(X)$ with respect to the norm $\|\phantom{a}\|$ as the sequence $(h_{m}(x))_{x\in\Gamma}$ converges in ${\mathbf{R}}^{\Gamma}$ and hence in every subspace.
L1014: It follows from Proposition 【34†7】 that a pluriharmonic function takes its maximum and its minimum on $\Gamma$ and hence $\|\phantom{a}\|$ is the sup-norm on $X$. We conclude that $h_{m}$ converges uniformly to $h$ on $X$ and hence $h=f$, proving the claim. ∎
